Subject: POC Kickoff Recap — Acme / Redwood

Hi Jared,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the clear overview of the support bot workload and the performance priorities. Per our discussion, here’s a concise recap and the proposed plan for the POC so we’re aligned on scope, success metrics, owners, and next steps.

High-level pain points you called out
- High latency during peak support hours (customer-facing bot experiences ~600–800ms 95th latency today)
- Token costs are a meaningful line item in the support org budget
- Occasional hallucinations for procedure-related prompts (false instructions are the main risk)

POC goals / success metrics
- Latency: target <= 200ms 95th for typical support queries (90–512 tokens)
- Cost: reduce per-response token cost by ~30% vs current hosted model via batching, adaptive quantization and caching
- Quality: measured by end-to-end accuracy on a 200-prompt eval set (no more than 3% regression vs baseline)

Scope (4 weeks)
- Integration: Connect Redwood API to your staging support backend (service account + S3 for traces)
- Prompt set & evals: Redwood will run the 200-prompt eval and share results; Acme will provide any proprietary labels for accuracy checks
- Performance tuning: batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles to hit latency/cost targets
- Rollout plan: validate in staging, then short canary to production if targets met

Owners
- Acme: Jared Lee (Product), Priya Singh (Ops) — provide access and sample traces
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AM), Aditya Rao (Platform Eng), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions)

Action items / next steps
1) Acme: grant a staging service account + S3 read access for traces (target by Wed 11/11)
2) Acme: share the 200-prompt eval set and current baseline metrics (by Wed 11/11)
3) Redwood: deliver POC scope doc and MVA checklist (attached) and schedule engineering sync (Aditya) — I’ll schedule for Thu 11/12 10am PT

Attachments
- redwood_mva_checklist.xlsx (POC readiness checklist)

If this looks right I’ll lock in the engineering sync and share the POC_Scope.pdf for signatures.

Thanks,

Hi all,

A few engineering notes to make the onboarding smooth — this is what we’ll cover in the Thu 11/12 sync and what I need from Acme to start.

Required access/setup (staging)
- Service account for Redwood with the following IAM permissions (or add aditya_rao@redwood.com as a principal): s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket on the provided traces bucket; if using AWS Cross-account role, share role ARN
- Sample traces: we need 3–5k representative request/response traces in JSONL (one record per line) — include token counts and latency timestamps
- Network: allow outbound calls to api.redwood.com from staging (whitelisted IPs will be provided)

POC infrastructure notes
- We will run the eval locally on Redwood infra; for latency testing we’ll run both internal synthetic load and replay of sampled traces
- Initial config: quantization profile (int8 where acceptable), conservative batch size to keep tail latency low, KV-prefix caching for repeated prefixes in support prompts

Deliverables from Redwood in week 1
- Baseline eval report (200 prompts) with accuracy/cost/latency
- MVA checklist (attached) and POC_Scope.pdf for signatures
- Engineering sync notes and next steps

Attachments referenced
